name: Matt Gaetz
role: U.S. Representative for Florida's 1st district (2017-2024); Florida state representative (2010-2016); One America News host
summary: A Republican populist who pushes limited government on spending, surveillance, guns and agencies (bills to abolish the EPA, ATF and USAID), non-interventionism abroad, restrictive immigration and social conservatism. He led the 2023 motion to vacate Speaker McCarthy over spending and process. He breaks from party orthodoxy on cannabis, war powers, ending forced arbitration and FISA.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted for the 2017 American Health Care Act (roll 256), which repealed major parts of the Affordable Care Act, and sponsored a bill making Medicaid conditional on work. No statement found favoring a state guarantee of coverage; his record runs the other way.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted No on the Raise the Wage Act in 2019 (roll 496), the bill to lift the federal minimum to $15.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (rolls 637 and 699) and cosponsored the Death Tax Repeal Act and the TCJA Permanency Act; no vote or bill of his raises taxes on high earners.

unions-good.rationale: Voted No on the PRO Act (2021 roll 70) and cosponsored the National Right-to-Work Act and the Davis-Bacon Repeal Act. His record opposes union-strengthening law; he was not found stating a view of unions themselves.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed record: wrote a bill to abolish the EPA and backs deregulation, but led Republicans in ending forced arbitration against big business, voted for it, and cosponsored antitrust bills aimed at large tech platforms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Sponsored the Medicaid Work Requirements Act and on the floor called a 2024 tax package a 'welfare bill masquerading as a tax bill' that expands the welfare state. He did not say welfare creates dependency, so +1.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Sponsored a resolution that FISA section 702 be allowed to expire, voted No on its 2024 reauthorization (roll 119) and told the House the FBI ran 278,000 'illegal queries' under it.

strong-leader.rationale: Argued Congress, not the executive, must decide war and spending, pressed to end 20-year-old national emergencies, and objected when the Biden administration went 'beyond what we set forth with our Article I powers'.

state-harmful.rationale: Described veterans, troops, Border Patrol and foreign operations funding as 'core functions of government'; he wants many agencies abolished but defends the defense, border and law-enforcement functions.

limit-guns.rationale: Wrote the Abolish the ATF Act and the Stand Your Ground Act, voted No on background-check bills (2019 roll 99, 2021 roll 75) and the Assault Weapons Ban (2022 roll 410), and voted for national concealed-carry reciprocity (2017 roll 663).

empower-police-military.rationale: Supports police (voted for National Police Week resolution and against the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act) and says military needs go unfunded, but he opposes Ukraine spending, a new FBI headquarters and Pentagon accounting failures, so the evidence is mixed.

decide-locally.rationale: Mixed: said police power belongs to the States and defended local management of a Florida sandbar, but also backed federal concealed-carry preemption, national constitutional carry and federal limits on birthright citizenship.

rehabilitation.rationale: Voted for the 2018 FIRST STEP Act (roll 215), which expanded prison programming and sentencing relief, but also voted No on the Prison to Proprietorship Act and has not spoken to the aim of prisons.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted No on the Respect for Marriage Act (2022 rolls 373 and 513) and on the Equality Act (2019, 2021); the first requires federal recognition of same-sex marriages. No direct statement on legality found.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted for the 20-week Pain-Capable Act (2017 roll 549) and Born-Alive Act, against the Women's Health Protection Act (2021 roll 295), cosponsored the Heartbeat Protection and Defund Planned Parenthood Acts, and referred to 'unborn lives and beating hearts' on the floor.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wrote the Protect Prayer in Schools Act, whose findings say the Constitution was 'never' meant to make the US secular, and cosponsored bills to protect Christmas symbols and religious services.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cosponsored bills to bar removal of state statues from the Capitol, to preserve the flag ('Old Glory Only'), and to protect Christmas symbols and traditions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called the Paris accord a 'globalist enterprise', argued US money should go to America's interests 'not to ... these global institutions', and cosponsored bills defunding the WHO and UN Human Rights Council.

nation-first.rationale: Said on the floor 'I am putting my countrymen first' in opposing more Ukraine aid and that 'a serious nation would never let foreign interests abroad ... dictate its foreign policy'.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposed US troop presence in Syria and Somalia and said the US 'cannot be the world's policeman', while describing Assad as a despot; his record is against rights-based intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Wrote border bills (ALIEN Act, BARRIER Act, End Birthright Citizenship Fraud Act), voted for the Secure the Border Act (2023 roll 209), and called border crossings an 'invasion'.

limit-growth.rationale: Said Paris-style climate commitments 'kill American jobs ... drive down our GDP' and that 'more prosperity' follows spending less; opposed trading growth for environmental targets.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His Green Real Deal resolution accepts climate risk and economy-wide emissions cuts through innovation and markets, but he voted No on the Climate Action Now Act (2019 roll 184) and later opposed the Paris accord.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His Green Real Deal resolution calls for investing in nuclear energy 'especially small modular reactors', and he voted for the Nuclear Energy Innovation and Modernization Act (2018 roll 493).

tax-inheritance.rationale: Cosponsored the Death Tax Repeal Act in the 117th and 118th Congresses, which ends the federal estate tax.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Cosponsored the 2024 Federal Reserve Board Abolition Act, which abolishes the Board and the Reserve banks and repeals the Federal Reserve Act. The bill does not say money is left to the market, so +1.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said 'I denounce political violence from all ends of the spectrum' yet on 6 January 2021 said 'I know there are many countries where political violence may be necessary, but America is not one such country'; mixed, leaning to not 'never'.

separate-church-state.rationale: His Protect Prayer in Schools Act states that 'the intent of the Constitution was never to render the United States a secular country' and that the Establishment Clause is being 'weaponized' against religion in schools.

military-superiority.rationale: Said America 'must hold the high ground' in the Indo-Pacific, that the US has 'fallen behind China' in hypersonics, and that US military needs are unfunded.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted No on the American Rescue Plan (2021 roll 49), Build Back Better (roll 385) and the Fiscal Responsibility Act (2023 roll 243), and called $33 trillion of debt and $2 trillion deficits 'chaos' and 'unsustainable'.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Wrote the Medicaid Work Requirements Act: from October 2023 no Medicaid for able-bodied adults who do not work 120 hours, volunteer 80 hours or join a work program.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted for the Lower Energy Costs Act (2023 roll 182) and his Green Real Deal resolution asks for 'fair and equal access to energy development on Federal lands'; his record on Gulf offshore drilling was not found.

national-mission.rationale: Mocked 'neo-conservative fantasy of turning an Arabian desert into a Jeffersonian democracy' and criticized trillions spent 'trying to build democracies out of sand and blood in the Middle East'.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Repeatedly described Washington's leadership as corrupt or untrustworthy: 'swampy logrolling', 'a grifter's gotta grift', leaders 'who do not deserve trust'.

separated-powers.rationale: Argued Congress must check the executive on war, spending and agency rulemaking ('Nobody voted for the ATF'; the executive may not go 'beyond what we set forth with our Article I powers').

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes government control of information: attacked a DHS disinformation board and monitoring of viewing habits, and cosponsored free-speech bills such as the Protecting Free Speech Act.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Held that Congress has a 'nondelegable duty' to decide war and peace and filed war powers resolutions directing troop removals, though he does not speak to who appoints ministers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pushed troop withdrawals from Syria and Somalia and complained Europe is subsidized, but voted to reaffirm NATO commitments in 2017 and did not call for ending alliances.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Wrote the End Birthright Citizenship Fraud Act: automatic birth citizenship only where a parent is a US national, refugee, permanent resident or service member, moving toward descent but keeping residence-based categories.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Wrote a bill to abolish USAID, offered an amendment to cut it by $4.5 billion and said 'I would take the USAID fund down to zero'; the US should not be 'the world's piggy bank'.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted Yea on a 2017 resolution reaffirming NATO's collective-defense commitment, but later voted No on the NATO Support Act (2019 roll 44) and on backing Finland and Sweden's NATO bids (2022 roll 364).

flat-income-tax.rationale: Said on the House floor in January 2024, 'We should have a flat tax code', and criticized targeted credits as distortions. He also cosponsored the FairTax, which replaces the income tax.

patriotic-education.rationale: Cosponsored the Saving American History Act, which says the federal government has a strong interest in forming 'knowledgeable and patriotic citizens' and bars funds for the 1619 curriculum.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Cosponsored the Puppy Protection Act, setting humane-treatment standards for dogs held by dealers.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Cosponsored the National Statuary Hall Collection Policy Act (no statue removal without two-thirds of the state delegation) and voted No in 2020 (roll 156) on replacing the Capitol bust of Roger Taney.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Objected on the floor that the Biden administration could not drain Army reserve funds beyond what Congress authorized and appropriated, 'beyond ... our Article I powers', and demanded use of 'the power of the purse'.

single-official-language.rationale: Cosponsored the English Language Unity Act, declaring English the official language of the United States; the bill stops short of ending all other-language services.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Cosponsored the 2022 National Security Moratorium on Foreign Purchases of U.S. Land, which prohibits foreign persons from buying US real estate.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Used Syria to criticize US arming of rebel groups, noting militias armed by the Pentagon fought those armed by the CIA, and sought withdrawal from that 'regime change' policy.

corporate-influence.rationale: Told the House that business tax credits are 'bought and paid for by the lobbyists who fund their campaigns' and sponsored the Lobbyist Accountability Act.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Voted No on the Equality Act in 2019 (roll 217) and 2021 (roll 39), which bars gender-identity discrimination, and cosponsored the End Taxpayer Funding of Gender Experimentation Act.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Was the Republican lead on the Forced Arbitration Injustice Repeal Act ('Article III courts ... ought to be good enough for big business') and voted Yea on the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act (2022 roll 33).

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

term-limits.rationale: Cosponsored the 2023 constitutional amendment limiting House members to three terms and told Speaker McCarthy he owed a floor vote on term limits under the January 2023 agreement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voted Yea on H.J.Res. 24 (2023 roll 118), disapproving the District of Columbia's Local Resident Voting Rights Amendment Act, which let noncitizen residents vote in local elections.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Voted Yea on affirming the United States record on the Armenian Genocide (2019 roll 591).

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Wrote the Stand Your Ground Act, which makes deadly force an affirmative defense when reasonably necessary to prevent death or great bodily harm to oneself or another, with no duty to retreat.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Opposed new wars and forever wars, yet backed the Soleimani killing and cited 'at times even preemptory self-defense'.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Voted No on the January 2024 Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act, and on the floor said refundable credits for people who pay no tax are 'welfare', not tax policy.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Faulted Speaker McCarthy for no floor vote on a balanced budget, which he said the January 2023 agreement required, and wants a top-line balanced-budget number set before appropriations.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Voted Yea twice in 2023 (rolls 234 and 277, the second a veto-override attempt) on H.J.Res. 45 to nullify the administration's student-loan waivers.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Cosponsored the English Language Unity Act, which sets a uniform English-language rule for naturalization.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cosponsored the 2021 National Right-to-Work Act, protecting an employee's choice to refrain from joining or paying a union.

voter-id.rationale: Voted Aye on the 2024 SAVE Act (roll 345), requiring proof of citizenship to register; this covers proof of citizenship, and he was not found speaking to ID at the polls.

close-ties-china.rationale: Wrote the No CHINA Act and the Securing Our Skies Against Chinese Technology Act and called China the rising threat, urging the US to counter its influence rather than seek closer ties.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Cosponsored the FairTax Act, which would replace income taxes with a national retail sales tax; this cuts against reducing sales taxes, but the bill's exemptions and offsetting repeal leave it ambiguous.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Told the House that targeted business tax credits are 'bought and paid for by the lobbyists who fund their campaigns', 'corporate welfare' and 'entirely wrong'.

notes: Evidence is his House record (roll calls, bills sponsored and cosponsored) and floor speeches in the Congressional Record, 2017-2024; his book and OAN-era interviews were not searched at length, so views stated only there are left null. Cannabis votes (MORE Act yes in 2020 and 2022, a bill to move marijuana to schedule III) are not answers to the all-drugs statement. Illegal-immigration measures are not answers to immigration levels or welfare for immigrants. The Green Real Deal resolutions (2019, 2021) and his later opposition to the Paris accord pull apart; the later position leads. Cosponsorships and single votes are capped at medium.
